newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen facing more profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen facing more profit-taking.

text.p: Profit-taking is expected to continue to afflict U.S. stocks on Friday but monthly durable goods orders data at 1230 GMT is expected to dictate the early pace.
Durable goods tend not to draw the kind of attention on a month-to-month basis that employment reports do because they can show wild fluctuations in any one period.
However, in a week that offered economists little in the way of new data, the report has grabbed centre stage.
"I find these numbers to be very quirky," said Larry Wachtel, market analyst at Prudential Securities.
Wall Street slipped again on Thursday. The Dow Jones industrial average ended below 6,000 for the first time in two weeks, down 43.98 points to 5,992.48.
